question.questionText: A: If she keeps up the good work she will be promoted to manager. B: I_________ so.
question.explanationHtml:
Detailed Explanation:

Other options either do not fit grammatically or are not commonly used in this context.
  • am hoping (verb phrase): Present continuous tense. Usually used for actions happening right now or around now, but not typically used in the fixed phrase 'I hope so.'
  • hope (verb): Simple present tense. Used to express a general wish or expectation. The correct and most natural choice in the phrase 'I hope so.'

  • will hope (verb phrase): Simple future tense. Used to talk about future intentions, but not used in the phrase 'I hope so.'
Related structure or vocabulary: The fixed phrase 'I hope so.' is used to express that you wish or expect something to happen. 'Hope' is used in the simple present tense in this phrase.
